howDoI.q: How do I make the hero glide on after a key is let go?

How do I make the hero turn around after a run?
How do I make a hop carry the hero forward?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Slide and Drift is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right add to Yana's speed, a little at a time. Space hops. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Hold a key and they get faster. Let go and they glide on, and slows. Nothing in this game can hurt you.

pages.head: Level 1: Glide
pages.html:
Level 1: Glide

TAP RIGHT AND LET GO. YANA GLIDES ON is the first sign. Tap Right and watch them slide a little after you lift your finger. HOLD IT LONGER AND THEY GO FASTER comes next: hold the key along the rink and they speed up, and glides farther when you let go. LET GO AND THEY SLOW. LEFT TURNS THEM AROUND is the last. Take the coins along the floor and walk into the door.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A step that adds speed. Open hero.chr in the Character tab and look at the sequence on the Right key. Its Momentum setting is on. A step with that setting does not move Yana by its frames' x. It adds the x to their speed, and their speed carries them on.
  • Faster while held. The first of the sequence's four frames adds 4, and the other three add nothing. The sequence repeats while the key is down, so they gain speed again and again.
  • Gliding on. When the key is let go, the sequence that runs is the standing one, which has no Momentum setting. The game then takes a sixth off their speed every tick until it is gone. A longer hold built up more, so the glide is longer.
  • Turning around. The Left sequence adds a push the other way, one step at a time, so they slow, stops and then goes back.
  • The map. Open one.map: a flat floor with a hedge at each end. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. A scene link joins the door to the next level in slide.gam.

pages.head: Level 2: Run-Up
pages.html:
Level 2: Run-Up

A HOP FROM STANDING GOES NOWHERE. HOLD RIGHT AS YOU HOP comes first. Hop with Space alone and Yana goes straight up and down. Three gaps follow, each wider than the last. A WIDER GAP NEEDS A RUN-UP FIRST and THE WIDEST. RUN, THEN HOP AT THE EDGE say how: run at the gap, press Space at its edge, and keep Right held until you land. Take the coins and walk into the door.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Speed rides a hop. The hop's own push is a Momentum step too, and it adds to the speed Yana already has. A run-up gives it speed to carry, and holding Right in the air keeps adding to it.
  • Sized by the map. Open two.map: the gaps are 5, 8 and 10 blocks wide. A hop with a short run covers about 9 blocks and with a long run about 12, so the widest gap needs the longest run.
  • No harm in falling. A gap is only two blocks deep, with ground at the bottom, so Yana lands in it and can hop out. Nothing is lost.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. The last door links to the The End scene in slide.gam.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot set a top speed. They move at most 11 pixels a tick. Their stored speed can climb higher, to 44, and a hold that long makes a longer glide before they slow to what you can see.
  • It cannot change how fast they slow. The game takes a sixth off each tick once no Momentum step is running. A different slide needs a block with a pull on it, as on ice.
  • It cannot brake with a key. A step with Momentum only adds speed, so pressing the other way slows them more slowly than letting go does. To stop, the player lets go.
  • It cannot let them slide into a wall. A solid block on their side takes all their speed at once, so there is no bounce or scrape.
  • It cannot give each key its own slide. All the steps with Momentum share one speed, and so do the hop and the glide.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Turn off Momentum on the Right sequence, and watch them stop the moment you let go.
  • Change the x of the first frame from 4 to 1, then to 8, and feel how hard each step pushes.
  • Widen the gaps in two.map until the run-up is not enough.
  • Draw a new frame for the glide, such as a skate or a sock slide.
  • Add a block with a pull to the floor and see how it adds to their glide.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer in a pink beanie has two levels to cross, and every step adds to their speed. Hold a key and they get faster, let go and they glide on, press the other way and they slow. In the second level a run-up carries a hop across wide gaps. Signs say what each level shows, and the manual says how each is made.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
Momentum is one setting on a sequence in the character file
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Two short levels about momentum. Every step Yana takes adds to their speed instead of moving them, so they get faster while a key is held and glides on after they let go. A wall stops them at once. In the second level, a hop made at speed carries across gaps a standing hop cannot. Nothing here hurts. Signs explain each idea, and every level has a page on how it is made.
